title: Unix datagram receive may retain a record after copy fault
mechanism: MessageReceiver::try_recv copies the front message to the user writer with ? before pop_front, so a copy fault returns EFAULT and leaves the message and its control data queued for the next receive.
contract: A non-peek Unix datagram receive consumes the selected datagram even if copying it to user memory fails (Linux unix_dgram_recvmsg).
observed: Source only: a copy fault returns EFAULT while the datagram stays at the queue head, so a retry receives it again.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes a faulting receive on a datagram socketpair followed by a valid retry, with MSG_PEEK as a control.

caveats: Source-only lead. Compare non-peek consumption and retry against Linux before calling it a defect. No security impact established.
